teaching_point: Classic AA: a well-defined, round, smooth, skin-coloured bald patch with NO scale, redness or scarring — follicular openings preserved (Day 1 case match).
dermnet_caption: A single patch of alopecia areata
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A single patch of alopecia areata (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alopecia-areata

teaching_point: Solitary vertex patch — often first noticed by a hairdresser or partner; limited (mild) disease = <20% scalp (SALT 1–20).
dermnet_caption: A single patch of alopecia areata on the vertex
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A single patch of alopecia areata on the vertex (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/alopecia-areata-images

teaching_point: Multifocal patchy AA — patches may enlarge and coalesce; document with photo + SALT at baseline (BAD R3/R4).
dermnet_caption: Several patches of alopecia areata on the scalp
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Several patches of alopecia areata on the scalp (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/alopecia-areata-images

teaching_point: Exclamation-mark hairs: short broken hairs that taper towards the scalp (narrow base, wider tip) at the active margin — near-diagnostic sign; the pull test is positive at the edge of an active patch.
dermnet_caption: Exclamation mark hairs at edge of patch
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Exclamation mark hairs at edge of patch (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alopecia-areata-in-children

teaching_point: Trichoscopy: exclamation-mark hairs (circled) — the tutor's 'most helpful finding' for Day 1.
dermnet_caption: Dermoscopic image of alopecia areata presenting with exclamation mark hairs
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopic image of alopecia areata presenting with exclamation mark hairs (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alopecia-areata

teaching_point: Other AA trichoscopy clues: yellow dots (keratin-filled ostia — proves follicles are still present = non-scarring), black dots (broken pigmented hairs), short vellus hairs.
dermnet_caption: Yellow dots, black dots, and short hairs
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Yellow dots, black dots, and short hairs (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alopecia-areata-in-children

teaching_point: Regrowth starts as fine, white/depigmented hairs — CKS: if regrowth is visible, no treatment is needed; colour usually returns (can be dyed).
dermnet_caption: Alopecia areata with fine hypopigmented regrowing hairs
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Alopecia areata with fine hypopigmented regrowing hairs (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/alopecia-areata-images

teaching_point: AA preferentially attacks pigmented hairs — white hairs are spared or regrow first (poliosis). Under-18s: specialist advice before potent steroids (CKS).
dermnet_caption: Patch alopecia areata with poliosis in a 14 year old
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Patch alopecia areata with poliosis in a 14 year old (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/alopecia-areata-images

teaching_point: Paediatric AA — DDx tinea capitis (scale, black dots, lymph nodes) and trichotillomania; refer/seek advice (CKS: children need specialist input).
dermnet_caption: Patchy alopecia areata in a child
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Patchy alopecia areata in a child (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alopecia-areata-in-children

teaching_point: AA can hit any hair-bearing site. Eyebrows: do NOT use potent topical steroids on the face — specialist intralesional triamcinolone is an option (BAD R21).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Eyebrow loss in alopecia areata (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alopecia-areata-in-children

teaching_point: Eyelash loss (madarosis) in AA — compare with trichotillomania (broken lashes of different lengths). Prostaglandin analogue to lash margin is specialist-only, if some hairs present (BAD R44).
caption_note: DermNet alt text 'Alopecia areata'; page title 'Madarosis due to alopecia areata'
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Alopecia areata (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/madarosis

teaching_point: Beard AA — round smooth patches in the beard; facial site = avoid potent steroids; DDx tinea barbae (inflamed, pustular).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Alopecia areata: beard (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/alopecia-areata-images

teaching_point: Ophiasis (band along the occipital/temporal margin) — poor prognostic sign; refer.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Ophiasic pattern alopecia areata (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alopecia-areata

teaching_point: Extensive patchy AA (moderate–severe, SALT ≥50 = severe) — specialist: DPCP, oral steroids/immunosuppressants, JAK inhibitor (ritlecitinib NICE TA958, age ≥12).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Extensive patchy alopecia areata (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alopecia-areata

teaching_point: Alopecia totalis (100% scalp) — ~1 in 10 chance of full recovery; specialist care + wigs (NHS wig via dermatologist); consider TFT + thyroid antibodies (BAD: notably in AT/AU).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Alopecia totalis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alopecia-areata

teaching_point: Nail pitting (fine, regular 'thimble' pits) — a simple bedside clue supporting AA and a marker of more severe/worse-prognosis disease.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Alopecia areata nail pitting (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alopecia-areata-in-children

teaching_point: Irregular, angular patch with hairs broken at many different lengths — not a smooth round patch; pull test negative.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Trichotillomania (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trichotillomania

teaching_point: Poorly defined area of thinning with stubble and broken hairs on the vertex/crown — reachable with the dominant hand.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption from page heading
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Trichotillomania (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trichotillomania

teaching_point: 'Tonsure' (Friar Tuck) pattern — crown/vertex loss with preserved margin; characteristic of chronic pulling.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption from image title on trichotillomania-images page
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Trichotillomania (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trichotillomania

teaching_point: Pulling/twisting behaviour — ask (non-judgementally) about automatic pulling while reading/screens vs focused pulling to relieve tension.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption from image title on trichotillomania-images page
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Trichotillomania (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trichotillomania

teaching_point: Frontotemporal/peri-auricular site on the side of the dominant hand — a classic trichotillomania distribution in children.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption from image title on trichotillomania-images page
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Trichotillomania (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trichotillomania

teaching_point: Pulling with excoriations/crusts — risk of secondary infection; repeated chronic pulling can damage follicles and leave permanent (scarring) loss.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption from image title on trichotillomania-images page
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Trichotillomania (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trichotillomania

teaching_point: Trichoscopy: black dots + broken hairs of uneven lengths, NO exclamation-mark hairs; other clues — flame hairs, V-sign, tulip hairs, split ends.
dermnet_caption: Trichotillomania showing black dots; follicular openings with remnants of pigmented hairs broken at scalp level
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Trichotillomania showing black dots; follicular openings with remnants of pigmented hairs broken at scalp level (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trichoscopy

teaching_point: V-sign — two hairs from one follicle snapped at the same level (pulled together): a trichotillomania-specific trichoscopy sign.
dermnet_caption: Trichotillomania showing V-sign that represents two hair shafts emerging from the same follicle and cut at the same level
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Trichotillomania showing V-sign that represents two hair shafts emerging from the same follicle and cut at the same level (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trichoscopy

teaching_point: Active scalp DLE: erythema + adherent scale + hair loss — inflammation in a bald patch is a red flag (AA is non-inflamed).
dermnet_caption: Erythema, scaling and alopecia in scalp discoid lupus erythematosus
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythema, scaling and alopecia in scalp discoid lupus erythematosus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/discoid-lupus-erythematosus-images

teaching_point: End-stage DLE — shiny, atrophic, depigmented/hyperpigmented scar with no follicular openings: hair will not regrow. Refer urgently.
dermnet_caption: Scarring alopecia due to discoid lupus erythematosus
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scarring alopecia due to discoid lupus erythematosus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus

teaching_point: Follicular keratotic plugs — a DLE clue on the scalp; also check ears (conchal bowl) and face.
dermnet_caption: Scarring alopecia with follicular plugging in discoid lupus erythematosus
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scarring alopecia with follicular plugging in discoid lupus erythematosus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/discoid-lupus-erythematosus-images

teaching_point: The core sign of ANY scarring alopecia: loss of follicular openings (ostia) on close/dermoscopic inspection.
dermnet_caption: Scarring alopecia with loss of follicular openings, sclerosis and telangiectatic vessels due to discoid lupus erythematosus
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scarring alopecia with loss of follicular openings, sclerosis and telangiectatic vessels due to discoid lupus erythematosus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/trichoscopy

teaching_point: LPP: smooth white patches without follicle openings; perifollicular redness and scale at the active edge (Day 1 tutor DDx).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lichen planopilaris (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lichen-planopilaris

teaching_point: Irregular, multifocal scarring patches that may coalesce — look for lichen planus elsewhere (mouth, nails, skin).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lichen planopilaris (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/hair-loss

teaching_point: LPP trichoscopy: perifollicular tubular scale/casts, erythema, absent ostia.
dermnet_caption: Dermoscopic image showing perifollicular scales (red circles, peritubular cast (black arrows) and blue grey dots (yellow circles)
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopic image showing perifollicular scales (red circles, peritubular cast (black arrows) and blue grey dots (yellow circles) (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lichen-planopilaris

teaching_point: FFA: band-like recession of the frontal (± temporal) hairline, pale shiny forehead skin, 'lonely' hairs — typically post-menopausal women. Do not dismiss as 'ageing'.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Frontal fibrosing alopecia (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/frontal-fibrosing-alopecia

teaching_point: Perifollicular erythema/scale along the hairline = active FFA → urgent referral to stop progression.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Note the perifollicular inflammation (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/frontal-fibrosing-alopecia

teaching_point: Eyebrow loss accompanying FFA — eyebrow loss in an older woman can be the first clue; DDx AA/trichotillomania/hypothyroidism.
caption_note: DermNet alt text 'Frontal fibrosing alopecia'; page title 'Madarosis due to frontal fibrosing alopecia'
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Frontal fibrosing alopecia (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/madarosis

teaching_point: Folliculitis decalvans: pustules, crusts, tufted ('doll's-hair') follicles at the vertex — swab pus, refer (neutrophilic scarring alopecia).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Tufted hairs and perifollicular crusting (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/folliculitis-decalvans

teaching_point: CCCA: shiny crown/vertex loss spreading outwards, mostly in women of African descent; ask about hair-care practices; refer early.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption from page heading
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/central-centrifugal-cicatricial-alopecia

teaching_point: Key AA mimic in children: tinea capitis — scaly 'grey patch' with broken hairs ± lymphadenopathy; take scalp scrapings + hair plucks for mycology before oral antifungal.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Grey patch scalp ringworm (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tinea-capitis

teaching_point: Black-dot tinea (T. tonsurans) — black dots mimic AA/trichotillomania; mycology settles it.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Black dot scalp ringworm (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tinea-capitis

teaching_point: Kerion — boggy, pustular inflamed plaque; can SCAR if untreated → urgent oral antifungal/specialist advice. Not a bacterial abscess (don't incise).
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption from page heading
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Tinea capitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tinea-capitis

teaching_point: Male AGA: bitemporal recession + vertex thinning, gradual over years, no bald 'patch', miniaturised hairs; pull test usually negative.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pattern balding (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/male-pattern-hair-loss

teaching_point: Advanced male pattern (Norwood high grade) — treatment is cosmetic: minoxidil OTC; finasteride 1 mg private only (MHRA 2024: psychiatric/sexual ADR alert card).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pattern balding (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/male-pattern-hair-loss

teaching_point: FPHL: diffuse crown thinning with widened central part and preserved frontal hairline (Day 1 tutor DDx). Check for androgen excess (PCOS) if irregular periods/acne/hirsutism.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Female pattern balding (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/hair-loss

teaching_point: Severe FPHL (Ludwig grade III) — topical minoxidil 2–5% (OTC) is first-line; set expectations (≥6–12 months; initial shedding).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Severe female pattern balding (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/hair-loss

teaching_point: Widening of the central parting ('Christmas-tree' pattern) — the simplest bedside sign of FPHL.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption from page heading
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Female pattern hair loss (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/female-pattern-hair-loss

teaching_point: TE: diffuse thinning all over, often 2–3 months after a trigger (illness, childbirth, crash diet, major stress, new drug); positive pull test diffusely; no patches.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Telogen effluvium (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/telogen-effluvium

teaching_point: Handfuls of shed club (telogen) hairs — the patient says 'it's coming out at the roots'; self-limiting within ~6 months once trigger removed. Check FBC, ferritin, TFT.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Hair shedding (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/telogen-effluvium

teaching_point: Traction alopecia (tight braids/weaves/ponytails) — marginal loss with 'fringe sign'; reversible early, scarring if prolonged. Ask about hairstyles.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Traction alopecia (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/traction-alopecia
